searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Fourteen were restricted to a house's or the Consejo's own domain (temposvegasicilia.com four times, familiafernandezrivera.com three, bodegasprotos.com four, aalto.es two, riberadelduero.es once) and are read as primary through their summaries; the other fourteen went to the open web for second sources (the Lecanda and Herrero years, the first Único, the founder of Pingus and the wreck, the vats, biodynamics, the dates of the founder of Tinto Pesquera, the Gran Reserva rule, the cession of the name, the Protos winery of 2008, Aalto's founders). Two of the open searches (the Gran Reserva rule and the cession of 1982) also returned the Consejo's and the ministry's own documents. One search, on the name Protos 5 Año, gave nothing. No WebFetch was tried. The allowance is spent, so whatever no search settled was cut or left open, never kept unsourced.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages for their own dates, vineyards and methods, then to the open web for the second source of each date and person, then to the Consejo Regulador's own documents for the Reserva and Gran Reserva rules and the history of 1982.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source (two unrelated Herreros, five to six years in wood for Único, fourteen months of American oak for the Pesquera Reserva, the co-operative of 1982, the vine ages and barrel months of PS); where the sources disagreed it was said with less (the early 1990s, old bush vines above all from two parcels); where no search found a detail it was cut (Bordeaux training, the myth clause, French oak at Pesquera, the bottle year, the tie of the 2008 winery to the galleries, Piñel de Abajo, Alión's place).
Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results but never cited in the fragment or here.

tested: Founded 1864, the library's year: the house's history (the son began to make wine professionally in 1864) and Wikipedia: confirmed.

1577, the name first written for the estate: the house's timeline and a brand guide repeating it; Wikipedia says the origin of the name is unknown and gives the older Pago de la Vega Santa Cecilia y Carrascal: kept, hedged as the house's account.
1848, the founder's father buying from the Marquis of Valbuena: the house's history; Wikipedia and others have the son inheriting in 1859: kept as the house's account, left open.

The Bordeaux cuttings of 1864, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Malbec: Wikipedia and a merchant's history (some add Carmenère and Pinot Noir, since lost): confirmed; the son's Bordeaux training was in no source: cut.
He was no trader: the house says the estate did not thrive for want of his skill as a trader and manager: confirmed.

1888 and 1897: the house names a first Herrero buyer of 1888, owner for less than ten years, and a second, no relative, who bought at auction in 1897 and whose family held it until 1950: the record's one family was wrong: changed.
1907, the Rioja merchant's lease and the Basque winemaker: the house's history; merchants give 1904 and 1905: kept as the house's telling, left open.
The first Único usually dated to the 1915 vintage: most accounts read (Fine and Rare, a Rare Wine Co article, merchants) give 1915, one 1914 or 1915: confirmed as worded.

1950 Prodes, 1965 the Venezuelan buyer of a Czech Jewish family who had tasted the wines in New York, April 1982 the Álvarez family: the house's history; 1982 also Liv-ex: confirmed, the word first cut.

The making: native yeasts in wooden vats with the malolactic in wood, barrels of 225 litres French and American, new and used, large wooden vats, at least ten years between barrel and bottle: the house's Único page and sheets: confirmed; six years in wood and four in bottle is the Único page's, about five years in oak the 2015 sheet's: changed to five to six.
Sites, 700 to 900 metres, fine colluvium with limestone fragments over sand and quartz gravel: the house's sheets: confirmed. Forty to sixty years of keeping: the house: confirmed.

Valbuena 5, named for five years between wood and bottle, Tinto Fino with 3 to 5 per cent Merlot: the house: confirmed, note and trap reworded. Reserva Especial, three vintages a release: a merchant's listing of the 2006 release (1989, 1990 and 1994): confirmed.
Alión: the house says the Álvarez family created it; its place near Peñafiel was not in any result: cut.
The respelling: Castilian says Sicilia with th: changed.
The questions: one right answer each, distractors of one kind; the story question's Herrero option is now plainly wrong for 1982 and the explanation says why: sound.
The house rules: nobody living named; no price, score or superlative; British; no dash: sound.

The first Tinto Pesquera of 1975, named for the founders' village: the family's Tinto Pesquera page, Wine Industry Advisor and Forbes España: confirmed.

The American critic's praise of the 1982 wines, likened to Pétrus: two accounts give the early 1980s and 1982 Tinto Pesquera, one 1985 and the Janus: kept as the middle of the 1980s, unnamed.

The Reserva rule, thirty six months with twelve in oak: the Consejo's Pliego: confirmed; the Gran Reserva, sixty months with twenty four in oak: the Consejo's guide and the ministry's Pliego modification: confirmed.
